# Sr Mechanical Engineer — Disneyland Resort

---
**Job ID:** 10161142
**Date Posted:** Sep 22, 2026
**Date Applied:** Sep 24, 2026
**Salary Range:** $115,300–$140,900 per year — Anaheim, CA (fully on-site)
---

## Job Summary

An Owner's Representative role in Architecture & Facilities Engineering (A&FE) at the Disneyland Resort. The engineer manages the full range of building mechanical systems (HVAC, central plant, and hydraulics/hydronics/compressed air), independently owns above- and below-ground mechanical utilities, and brings kitchen and food-and-beverage expertise across attraction buildings, hotels, restaurants, retail, offices, and backstage infrastructure. The role reports to the Manager, MEP Engineering.

---

## What You'll Do

- Act as Owner's Representative on mechanical projects from concept through construction.
- Manage design and contract documents with in-house and outside resources to meet scope, schedule, and budget.
- Coordinate design activities and monitor field installations and demolition for specification and code compliance.
- Develop concept designs and support RFPs for external design and consulting services.
- Respond to urgent reactionary projects.
- Own the full above- and below-ground mechanical utility scope and lead kitchen design coordination for back-of-house and guest-visible ("show") kitchens.
- Review drawings, calculations, and specifications against local and state codes; review shop drawing submittals and respond to vendor RFIs.
- Conduct site visits to solve issues and minimize schedule impacts.
- Witness signing and sealing of construction documents, and mentor less experienced colleagues and interns.

### Required Qualifications
- 5+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience
- Strong working knowledge of the California Mechanical Code, ASHRAE standards, and the California Energy Code (Title 24)
- Demonstrated ability to motivate and oversee others, including interns
- Strong problem-solving skills for unfamiliar issues
- Demonstrated ability to own complex mechanical utility scopes and lead design coordination across stakeholders
- Experience with design, procurement, and logistics in a team environment
- Preferred: Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field and/or MBA, Disneyland College Program or internship experience, and experience with other Disneyland Resort lines of business

### Education
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field from an ABET-accredited university, plus a **current Professional Engineer (PE) license** (required).

### Benefits
Disney's rewards package (health and savings benefits, educational opportunities, and Disney extras). A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be included, depending on level and position offered.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Sep 24, 2026

- **The PE license is a hard gap:** the posting requires a current Professional Engineer license, and the record lists none. This is the deciding requirement for this role.
- **Building-systems codes are not in the record:** there is no evidence for HVAC, central plant, hydronics, the California Mechanical Code, ASHRAE, Title 24, or construction-document and RFI workflows. Riley's mechanical work is product and machine design, not building MEP.
- **Transferable mechanical and coordination strengths:** thermal and acoustic enclosure redesign, custom AC heaters on the ICARUS-Lite, fixture and tooling design, GD&T, DFM/DFA, and custom tooling with local fabricators for large-radius aluminum bends support the design side. Vendor communication and cost negotiation, sourcing, and fabrication management (THE KRAKEN) support the design/procurement/logistics requirement.
- **Leadership overlap:** acting as Hiring Manager for engineering roles and leading R&D covers the "motivate and oversee others" requirement.
- **Education:** the B.S. in Electro-Mechanical Engineering (Penn State) is a related field. ABET accreditation isn't recorded in the site data.

### Now — Sep 24, 2026

- No change since application (applied today).
